ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a water pump three-phase motor control circuit, with the main circuit on the left and the control circuit on the right. In the main circuit, it can be seen that the three-phase power supply enters the contactor circuit after passing through QS and FU1, and below there are the thermal relay FR and the three-phase motor M. In the main circuit, two groups of contactor contacts labeled KM1 and KM2 are marked, and in the branch leading to the motor stator circuit there are three resistor elements labeled R. In the control circuit on the right, there are coils and auxiliary contacts such as SB1, SB2, FR normally closed protection contact, KM1, KT, and KM2, used to control contactor actions in time sequence. Reasoning: Since during starting, resistors labeled R are connected in series into the motor stator circuit, the voltage applied to the stator winding is reduced; afterward another group of contactor contacts acts to remove or bypass the series resistors, causing the motor to enter normal operation. Therefore, this starting method belongs to stator winding series-resistance reduced-voltage starting.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: identify it as a water-pump three-phase motor control circuit with a power section and a control section. In the power section, locate motor M, thermal relay FR, contactors KM1 and KM2, and the resistor elements labeled R connected in the stator supply path. Observe that the starting path places R in series with the motor stator windings, while another contactor path subsequently removes/bypasses R. Then apply the standard classification of motor reduced-voltage starts: series impedance in the stator circuit means stator series-resistor voltage reduction. Fill the blank as 'stator winding series resistor voltage reduction start.'
